sessions.label: Practice 1
narrative: Charles Leclerc set the pace in Practice 1 with a 1:23.008.

Esteban Ocon left the most time on the table: their fastest lap (1:25.852) was 0.419s slower than the theoretical lap built from their own best sectors (1:25.433), so there is more pace in the car than the lap time shows.
Paul Aron had the highest speed-trap reading, 341.0 km/h.
On long runs, Luke Browning's SOFT-tyre stint (stint 4, 10 laps) had the best clean average pace at 84.989s/lap (slowest lap of the stint dropped as an outlier).

Context on Charles Leclerc's pace: “Charles Leclerc was only 1.3s away from the podium in Zandvoort, but finished fifth in the final Dutch Grand Prix despite Ferrari demonstrating plenty of race pace on Sunday. The Monegasque driver had an eventful...” (— Charles Leclerc rues bad luck in Zandvoort but admits race was lost thanks to starting position, Formula1.com).

Context on Luke Browning's long-run pace: “Luke Browning to drive for Williams in FP1 at the Italian Grand Prix” (— Luke Browning to drive for Williams in FP1 at the Italian Grand Prix, Formula1.com).
